newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Foreigners interest seen rising in Kazakh T-bills.
newsitem.headline: Foreigners interest seen rising in Kazakh T-bills.

text.p: The yield on Kazakh six-month Treasury bills (GKOs) should fall next week as foreign demand steps up, while yields on the three-month paper are likely to remain unchanged, dealers said.
Kazakhstan's Finance Ministry is offering T-bills worth a total of 670 million tenge for an auction on Monday, followed by three-month bills worth a total of 650 million on Tuesday.
"I expect the yield on six-month bills will fall due to big demand by investors, especially foreign ones," said Oleg Tsurkan, head treasurer at ABN AMRO Bank Kazakhstan.
Tsurkan said he expected the yield to fall by around one point. The six-month paper yielded 27.76 percent annual at the previous auction on February 17.
Another dealer noted growing activity from Russian banks who are looking to the Kazakh debt market after Russia introduced a 15-percent tax on domestic T-bill operations.

At the previous auction of three-month T-bills on Tuesday their yield rose to 24.36 percent annual from 23.06 percent at an auction last week, and dealers say yields will fluctuate only a little around the current yield.
Dealers said yields on three-month GKOs could start rising later in March.

Last December the Finance Ministry suspended issuing three-month T-bills because it had received enough money to bridge the budget gap from a successful placement of Kazakh Eurobonds on international financial markets.

TexaKaBank dealer Daniyar Amangeldin said no three-month GKOs would be redeemed in March. "There appears to be an empty niche but a lot will depend on the National Bank which issues 14- and 28-day notes to regulate money supply," he said.
The notes yields about 30 percent annual.
